summary: Opaque tenant spike causing slot-locks and autoscaler starvation in reserved GPU pool
description:
Issue summary:
During the 2026-03-10 09:40-10:15 UTC window NimbusDocs observed a sharp p99/p95 latency and throughput degradation on their reserved GPU pool. The customer's traffic pattern shows many short streaming requests that were previously stable. Impact: customer-facing inference endpoints experienced 40-60% throughput drop and p99 latency increased from ~420ms to >2.5s.

Impact:
- NimbusDocs production (dedicated pool) saw degraded throughput and intermittent 5xx errors for inference routes pinned to llama-3-70b and redwood-instruct-13b.
- Some requests were stuck in queue for >30s until kernel allocation failed and returned 503.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: rp-nimbus-west-1 (prod-us-west)
- Pool allocation: 8xA100 (mixed mixed-memory minor mismatch), autoscaler configured with min=6 max=12, slot-size=1 GPU per slot.

Steps to reproduce (how customer triggered):
1) Customer sent a short-burst test (many small streams) starting at 09:40 UTC with synthetic traffic similar to production (avg token count 20-40).
2) Within ~3 minutes we saw queue growth at the pool scheduler and preemption/lease retries.
3) Throughput dropped despite autoscaler triggers.

Observed behavior:
- Scheduler shows multiple slots entering a "locked" state where in-use flag prevents new batch assignment for 10-30s.
- Autoscaler did fire scale-up events but new GPUs were slow to accept tasks due to slot lock propagation.
- No explicit OOM on GPUs; device utilization was inconsistent (some GPUs at 95% while others idle).

Request: Please investigate root cause of slot lock behavior, why autoscaler scale-up did not recover throughput quickly, and provide mitigation for NimbusDocs.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:05 - Aisha Patel (Support): Initial alert from customer. Captured stack traces and dashboard links; escalating to SRE.
2026-03-10 10:20 - Liam Chen (SRE): Reproduced queue growth on rp-nimbus-west-1. Noticed multiple scheduler lease retries (kube-scheduler-like lease pattern). Collecting gpu daemon and sidecar logs.

2026-03-10 11:02 - Maya Ortiz (Infra): Applied temporary throttling to the customer's API keys to reduce short-stream fanout. Observed queue drain within ~7 minutes. Customer confirmed latency returned to baseline.
2026-03-11 09:15 - Liam Chen (SRE): Follow-up: we triggered an emergency add of 2 spare GPUs to pool and reduced slot-timeout to 30s to limit slot locking. Adding investigation notes to ticket.
investigation_notes:
Logs and metrics reviewed:
- Scheduler logs (2026-03-10 09:38-10:12 UTC): repeated 'slot_acquire_timeout' events (~1800 occurrences). Lease renewal attempts showed exponential backoff.
- Sidecar logs: several sidecars reported transient IPC timeouts when attempting to serialize small streaming batches.
- GPU telemetry: per-GPU NVLink and PCI stats show bursts of host-to-device transfer followed by long idle windows on some cards.
- KV cache metrics: no significant growth.
- Network: up to 2% packet retransmits between host and GPU nodes during the window.

Hypothesis:
1) A silent tenant (not NimbusDocs) generated a high rate of very-short streaming requests which caused frequent context switches in serving runtime. That combined with a scheduling bug led to slot objects being held (slot-lock) while sidecars retried IPC calls. The held slot prevented the scheduler from assigning new micro-batches to idle GPUs, creating effective starvation.
2) Autoscaler reacted correctly but new GPUs could not accept assignments until lock states propagated out of the scheduler's in-memory structures, causing slow recovery.

Evidence for hypothesis:
- Correlated increase in 'short_stream_count' metric across the entire host cluster at same timestamp.
- Heap and lock contention traces show prolonged hold on slot mutex in serving-runtime thread.
- Affected nodes have both high GPU utilization and high scheduler queue depth, indicating uneven work distribution.

Telemetry & links:
- Dashboard: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/rp/nimbus-west-1/overview?from=2026-03-10T09:30Z&to=2026-03-10T10:30Z
- Scheduler logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/streams/slot_lock_20260310
- Sidecar traces (sampled): https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/3f2a7b"
mitigation:
Immediate mitigations applied on 2026-03-10:
- Throttled noisy API keys suspected of fanout (temporary rate limit applied by Support).
- Added 2 spare GPUs to the pool to provide headroom.
- Reduced slot-timeout from 90s -> 30s for the pool to accelerate slot reclamation.
- Deployed a temporary hotfix disabling one path of synchronous sidecar IPC for small streaming batches (bypass mode).
Result: throughput recovered to ~95% of baseline within 7-10 minutes after mitigations. Customer confirmed service level improved and no further 5xxs were observed after 10:30 UTC.
resolution:
Workaround applied and validated: customer traffic is stable after throttling and slot-timeout tuning. Temporary hotfix reduced sidecar blocking for short streams. Root cause suspected to be a combination of short-stream fanout and a scheduler slot-lock bug.

Status: Mitigation in place; permanent fix pending. Assigned to eng-team-serving for a code-level remediation and autoscaler-resilience changes. Scheduled postmortem and rollout plan.
next_steps:
Short-term (1-3 days):
- ENG SERVE: revert bypass after full fix validated, instrument slot lock counters more aggressively (owner: Priya Rao).
- ENG AUTOSCALE: add faster reconciliation path for new nodes and a protective guard that allows redistribution when slot locks detected (owner: Marco Silva).
- Support: coordinate customer communication and provide detailed timeline for permanent fix (owner: Aisha Patel).

Medium-term (2-4 weeks):
- Root-cause PR to fix slot mutex path and reduce blocking in sidecar IPC (PR target: infra#3892).
- Add alert: sustained short_stream_count > threshold AND slot_acquire_timeout > X should auto-trigger a protective throttle or pool soft-scale up.

Postmortem: schedule for 2026-03-17. Deliverables: postmortem doc, code PRs, and an RCA.
